title: Customer research: who to learn from, and interviews vs survey
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Which customers to learn from for a given decision, which method fits the pool size, and how to turn coded answers into one chosen Job.
applies_when: Finding why people stall or leave
Few customers and no usable analytics
exclusions: No consented way to contact customers (use public sources instead)
required_inputs: Customer list with consent to contact
The decision the research must inform
evidence_requirements: List of paying customers with start date
A value-realized signal per customer (usage, renewals, repeat orders, owner judgement)
Consent basis to contact customers for research
Coded research answers (K1/K2) with respondent IDs
Per-Job signals for urgency, willingness to pay, support burden, retention, expansion, reachability
15+ interviews per stage with target customers (not friends)
missing_data_behavior: Small pool: census of recent best-fit payers; no percentages.
No customers yet: problem interviews with prospects (PB-interviews, Mom Test rules).

decision_branches.then: Recent best-fit payers (about the last 12 months).

decision_branches.if: Decision is why people drop off
decision_branches.then: Contrast groups: stalled, churned, didn't buy.

decision_branches.if: Pool large enough for a survey (authors' rule of thumb about 500)
decision_branches.then: Short survey plus a few interviews; counts rank themes within the sample only.

implementation_steps: Filter customers: felt the problem, pay without hesitation, ongoing need, value realized, started 3-6 months ago (up to 12)
Count the pool and choose method
Ask what happened in sequence (old way, trigger, search, choice, certainty moment, new capability)
Keep raw answers with respondent counts
Tag every answer with struggle, motivation and desired-outcome themes, one dimension at a time
Count struggle themes as n of N respondents
For each top struggle, filter to its respondents and count their motivations and outcomes
Run a script: context, ranking, how they solve it now.
Ask for a commitment (follow-up, intro, pre-order).
dependencies: At least some customers who have solved their problem with the product
A named decision the research must inform (Book 02 §1)
At least ~10 coded respondents, or labelled thin
a script that separates problem from solution

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: Owner 5-10 hours for 10-15 interviews; less for a survey
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: Contact list, survey form or calendar
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Respondent and invite counts; response rate

metrics: Share of answers that describe events rather than opinions
Conditional share of motivation within a struggle
After choosing: signup and first-value rates for the chosen Job's traffic
share of interviews with an existing workaround
guardrails: Commitments outweigh enthusiasm (Mom Test over interview-scoring rubrics).
Theme counts are not prevalence estimates.
No synthetic respondents or invented quotes
Owner approves every send; sends only from owner's channels with a consent basis
Every theme count shows n of N and pool
Criteria scores cite evidence or say unknown
never quote an interviewee publicly without consent
no cold outreach via ClimbOS's own email service for recruitment
alternatives_when_constrained: No list or consent: audience research (BK08-K2) or public review mining (voc-research)
Tiny pool (<10 best customers): 3-5 interviews plus competitor reviews, labelled thin
No research: owner's notes from 5 best clients coded the same way, labelled owner-reported
Very small sample: keep Jobs as hypotheses and test messages per Job in ads or email
can't find 15 people: treat that as a reachability warning; use paid research panels or existing customers
stop_conditions: Survey under 10 usable answers after 14 days: switch to interviews (CH-C2)
Interviews stop adding new struggle themes: stop
Answers scattered across many Jobs after ~10: narrow the segment (PB-interviews revise)
Chosen Job's messaging shows no change in signup or first-value rate after the planned window: revisit choice or execution
New research shows the Job's trigger changed: redo
after 15 interviews per segment, decide: proceed, narrow segment, or drop
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Only happy customers interviewed for a churn question (selection bias)
Long-tenured customers cannot recall the trigger
Trying to serve all Jobs at once (book's top mistake)
Scoring body language is subjective; weight commitments more.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: PB-interviews v2 chooses the recruitment pool from the decision: best-fit recent payers for targeting/messaging decisions; contrast pools (stalled, churned, non-buyers) for activation/conversion/retention diagnoses.
proposed: voc-research outputs 2-3 Job statements built from the conditional cross-tab, each with n of N, and a one-Job recommendation with the runner-up.
proposed: when the most frequent Job is not the best on payment, retention or reachability, show both and let the owner choose.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: the 500-customer survey threshold and 10-15% response rate are shown as author heuristics, never as expected yields; the plan uses the owner's own list size and states the assumed rate.
proposed: participants should have started paying within about 12 months so they can recall the trigger; older customers go in a separate pool.
proposed: a Job statement needs a struggle theme seen in at least 3 respondents from the same pool (matches voc-research 'finding' bar).
proposed: PB-interviews readouts tally three things per interview, existing workaround, commitment offered, unprompted mention, and report counts by segment; any numeric score is labelled subjective.

external_requirement.rule: proposed: no research send without a recorded consent basis and owner approval.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: theme percentages and conditional shares are computed in code from coded rows, never written by the model.

reconciliation_note: Book 02 recruits contrast groups; Forget the Funnel recruits best-fit customers. The decision decides (RECONCILIATION R10).
